Definition: Anah, the name of two Edomites and one Edomitess
BiblicalUsage: Three people share the name Anah, and the Bible keeps them apart by their fathers: Anah the daughter of Zibeon became one of Esau's wives, Anah the son of Zibeon is the one who found the mules in the wilderness as he fed his father's asses, and Anah the son of Seir is named among the Horite chiefs of Edom. The lists give us the names and the families, and nothing more.
TheologicalSignificance: Three people, one name, and no confusion in the record: the Bible names each Anah by their father and their place. I believe that is how carefully God keeps His people's names — even the ones we only meet in a genealogy.
